objectives.label: Resources of collecting data
objectives.description: Distinguish primary resources from secondary resources of collecting data and state the advantages of each.

objectives.label: Methods of collecting data
objectives.description: Identify the method of collecting data (method of mass population or method of samples) suited to the aim and size of the statistical society, stating its advantages and disadvantages.

objectives.label: Selecting types of samples
objectives.description: Select a sample using a biased choice, a simple random sample or a layer sample, and decide how many units to take from each layer.

passages.text: The method of collecting data is considered one of the most important phases that statistical research mainly depends on. Collecting data in such scientific methods will lead to get accurate outcomes when doing operations of statistical inferrence and proper decision making.

A.why: Opens the lesson by saying why collecting data matters for accurate statistical results.

B.why: Explains why collecting data matters to the whole lesson: accurate outcomes and sound decisions.

passages.text: The method of collecting data is determined according to the aim and the size of the statistical society under study.

A.why: States that the method depends on the aim and size of the statistical society.

B.why: Says the method of collecting data depends on the aim and size of the society.

passages.text: For example: The students of a school represent a statistical society whose value is the student.

A.why: A short example defining a statistical society, with no motivating situation.

B.why: Students of a school as a statistical society is a picturable example.

passages.text: The disadvantages of such a method are: it needs long time and great efforts. Furthermore, it costs much money.

A.why: A side note listing the disadvantages of a method.

B.why: States the disadvantages of a method, a detail of the content, not an introduction.

passages.text: It mainly depends upon selecting a sample from the statistical society that it represents.

A.why: Explains what the sample method is: choosing a sample from the society.

B.why: Says what the sample method depends on: choosing a sample that represents the society.

passages.text: We conduct researches on the sample. The outcomes we get are generalized on the whole society.

A.why: Describes the procedure of the sample method, not a why or a situation.

B.why: A statement of how sample results are used, not a motivating situation or question.

passages.text: For example, when we want to know how the students understood a lesson in mathematics we must analyze the outcomes of the test by considering the outcomes of a group of students studied the same topic without the other students; this is not a random selection.

A.why: Students' maths test results from one group show a biased, non-random choice that a student can picture.

B.why: Picture testing only one group of students to judge a lesson, an example of a biased, non-random choice.

passages.text: Of the most important types of the random samples:

A.why: A lead-in to a list of sample types.

B.why: A lead-in to a list of random sample types, not a motivating idea.

passages.text: Repeat pressing on the = key; the appearance of numbers will be successive.

A.why: A calculator instruction.

B.why: A calculator instruction for generating random numbers.

passages.text: For example: to study the educational level of a society of 400 persons where the ratio of males to females is 3:2, with a sample of 50 persons, we must select 30 persons from the male layer and 20 persons from the female layer randomly.

A.why: A worked example of the layer-sample method with numbers.

B.why: A worked example of stratified sampling with numbers, not an introduction.

objectives.label: Range as dispersion
objectives.description: Calculate the range of a set of values (greatest value minus smallest value) and use it, with the mean, to compare the dispersion of two sets.

objectives.label: Standard deviation of values
objectives.description: Calculate the standard deviation of a set of values using the mean and the squared deviations from the mean.

objectives.label: Standard deviation of frequency distributions
objectives.description: Calculate the mean and standard deviation of a frequency distribution, including grouped sets using the centres of the sets.

objectives.label: Compare homogeneity by standard deviation
objectives.description: Decide which of two distributions is more homogeneous by comparing their standard deviations (the larger standard deviation is more dispersed), representing them with a frequency polygon.

passages.text: If the weekly wages in pounds of two sets of workers A and B in a factory are as follows: Set A: 170, 180, 180, 230, 240; Set B: 50, 180, 180, 190, 400

A.why: Two sets of factory workers with weekly wages set up the idea of dispersion for the whole lesson.

B.why: Weekly wages of two sets of factory workers is a situation a student can picture, used to motivate range and dispersion.

passages.placed: the whole lesson: the readings named it and one objective

A.why: Worked calculation of the two means.

B.why: Worked calculation of the means.

passages.text: Compare the wages of the two sets A and B to find :

A.why: An instruction to compare the sets.

B.why: Instruction to compare the sets.

passages.text: 1. The mean of wages for set A = the mean of wages of set B = LE 200

A.why: A step stating the equal means.

B.why: Worked result stating equal means.

passages.text: 2. The median of wages = the mode wage = LE 180 for each set A and B

A.why: A step stating the equal median and mode.

B.why: Worked result stating median and mode.

passages.text: (1) The wages of the two sets are different but both have the same measures of central tendency.

A.why: A conclusion of the comparison, not a motivating question.

B.why: Step of the worked comparison.

passages.text: (2) The wages of set A are close so the values are included between 170 and 240 pounds where the wages of set B are divergent so the values are included between 50 and 400 pounds.

A.why: A step of the comparison using the ranges of the values.

B.why: Step of the worked comparison with the wage ranges.

passages.text: i.e. The wages of set B is more divergent than the wages of set A.

A.why: A conclusion statement of the comparison.

B.why: Conclusion step of the worked solution.

passages.text: So When we compare two sets, we must consider the dispersion of the values of both sets and being divergent from each other.

A.why: States why we must consider the dispersion of values when comparing two sets, which leads to the range.

B.why: States why dispersion must be considered when comparing two sets, with no worked numbers.

passages.text: The mean $\bar{x} = \frac{504}{40} = 12.6$
